question: Our contract manufacturer rejected a batch of eye shadow for microbial contamination. Can we rework it, and does any FDA rule govern the reprocessing?
answer: The FDA requires that contract manufacturers must ensure that all operations in receiving, inspecting, transporting, segregating, preparing, manufacturing, packaging, and storing of food comply with sanitation principles. If any food becomes contaminated, it shall be rejected, or if permissible, treated or processed to eliminate the contamination. If applicable, the FDA guidance requires that the contract manufacturer must have a procedure in place for receiving information from the contract facility on all deviations, complaints, and adverse events. If applicable, the FDA guidance also requires that the contract manufacturer must have access to floor plans, equipment validation, and other production information.

sources.heading: Processes and controls.
sources.text: All operations in the receiving, inspecting, transporting, segregating, preparing, manufacturing, packaging, and storing of food shall be conducted in accordance with adequate sanitation principles. Appropriate quality control operations shall be employed to ensure that food is suitable for human consumption and that food-packaging materials are safe and suitable. Overall sanitation of the plant shall be under the supervision of one or more competent individuals assigned responsibility for this function. All reasonable precautions shall be taken to ensure that production procedures do not contribute contamination from any source. Chemical, microbial, or extraneous-material testing procedures shall be used where necessary to identify sanitation failures or possible food contamination. All food that has become contaminated to the extent that it is adulterated within the meaning of the act shall be rejected, or if permissible, treated or processed to eliminate the contamination.
